key_insight: A symmetry-aware variational framework can simulate the finite-size Dicke model on both digital qubit devices and hybrid qubit-boson hardware while reproducing the model’s characteristic critical behavior in the large-spin limit.
engineering_relevance: The approach points to more resource-efficient quantum simulation workflows for collective light-matter systems on near-term quantum hardware, including trapped-ion and hybrid platforms.
method: Developed a variational formulation for the finite-size Dicke model on fully qubit-based digital quantum computers.
Introduced a hybrid qubit-bosonic variational ansatz that uses the bosonic mode directly to reduce quantum resources.
Validated the framework against classical emulators and discussed extension to more general spin-boson models.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model reproduces Dicke critical behavior in the appropriate large-spin limit and is suitable for both classical emulation and trapped-ion implementation, though hardware noise affects performance.
watch_item: Implementation on current trapped-ion hardware is limited by noise, which may reduce accuracy relative to emulator results.
paper_title: Simulating the Dicke Model on Qubit-Based and hybrid Qubit-Boson-Based Quantum Computers
